issues.legal_issue: A village held under a permanent under-tenure is excluded from classification as a zamindari estate even when it is physically included in a zamindari.
material_facts: A village was granted permanently as a hereditary holding, subject to payment of dues.
At the permanent settlement, the office associated with the grant was abolished but the grant itself was maintained.
The settlement transferred the ultimate reversionary interest to the zamindar, who became an intermediary between the government and the holder.
The village’s continuing tenure was therefore under the zamindar, although records and descriptions sometimes associated it with the zamindari.
The government notified the village as a zamindari estate, and the holder challenged that notification.
issues.conclusion: The village was held under a permanent under-tenure, not as a zamindari estate. The notification classifying it as a zamindari estate was void, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(2)(e) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, a portion of specified estates held on a permanent under-tenure is an estate; under sections 2(3) and 2(15) of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, it is an under-tenure estate. Section 2(16) excludes an under-tenure estate from the definition of a zamindari estate. Whether a grant is pre-settlement or post-settlement is immaterial; the material consideration is where the reversionary interest rests. Inclusion of a village in a zamindari, or its description as a zamindari village, does not by itself determine its statutory classification. The Court referred to Gopisetti Veeraswami v. Sagiraju Seetharama Kantayya (1926) and Narayanaswami Bahadur v. Boda Thammayya (1930).

rule.if: challenge_to_zamindari_notification and permanent_hereditary_village_grant and grant_tenure_continued_after_settlement and reversionary_interest_in_proprietor and proprietor_interposed_as_intermediary

predicates.challenge_to_zamindari_notification: The proceeding challenges a government notification classifying a holding as a zamindari estate.
predicates.permanent_hereditary_village_grant: A village was granted as a permanent hereditary holding.
predicates.grant_tenure_continued_after_settlement: The tenure created by the grant continued after the permanent settlement.
predicates.reversionary_interest_in_proprietor: The ultimate reversionary interest in the village rested with the proprietor.
predicates.proprietor_interposed_as_intermediary: The proprietor stood between the government and the holder of the village.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a zamindari notification and the village was permanently granted, the grant continued after settlement, and the proprietor held the reversionary interest as an intermediary, the notification is void.
